messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: embeddings-api-high-5xx (sev2) — multiple customers reporting 503s from /v1/embeddings. Alerting rules: p95 5xx > 2% over 5m. Links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/emb-503-1769987654
Alyssa: seeing ~2.8% 5xx at the edge, spikes aligned with autoscaler thrash on embeddings-autoscaler. Some pods OOMing and restarting.
Alyssa: quick check — rolling update started ~10:12 UTC, autoscaler scaled to 0 then back to 12 rapidly.
Praveen K: I saw same, traced to kv-cache leader evictions causing backend latency and upstream timeouts.
Tess R: customer impact: 3 high-tier customers experienced degraded embeddings for ~8 minutes. Support already pinged them.
Alyssa: mitigation steps taken so far:
- disabled aggressive embedding autoscaler policy for eu-west (set minReplicas=4)
- cordoned and drained 2 suspect nodes (nodepool-emb-3) to stop noisy hardware interference
- enabled fallback model route: embeddings-small for requests to high-latency tenants
- bumped ember-cache TTL to 60s while we stabilize
(used commands below)
```
kubectl -n embeddings patch hpa embeddings-autoscaler --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}'
kubectl cordon nodepool-emb-3-0
kubectl drain nodepool-emb-3-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Mike S: thanks, Alyssa. After cordoning nodes 5xx dropped to 0.7% and tail latency improved. Still watching memory pressure on a few hosts.
deploy-bot: deploy roll-forward of ember-cache ttl=60s succeeded (deploy-id dpl_2026_04_06_1017).
Alyssa: current status: incident considered mitigated for now, customers on fallback route, autoscaler policy relaxed.
Tess R: open items for next shift: validate nodepool health, verify kernel oom logs for drained nodes, revert fallback after confirm no regressions.
Praveen K: I'll take post-incident diagnostics: collecting GC/oom logs and edge traces, will post artifacts to the incident folder.
Alyssa: runbook references: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-autoscaler and https://docs.redwood/playbooks/kv-cache-eviction — see section "Mitigation: temporary minReplicas" for exact commands.
Tess R: coverage for next 12h — primary: Mike S, secondary: Tess R (swap in 6h if overlap). Oncall rotations note: Alyssa -> Mike S handoff completes at 11:00 UTC.
Mike S: I can take primary. Availability: online, phone with me. Will check memory/oom, reinstatement plan for fallback.
Alyssa: coverage gap: no infra person scheduled for 18:00-19:00 UTC tomorrow — we should flag to eng-sre to cover.
Praveen K: follow-ups assigned:
- Praveen: collect kernel & oom logs, dump docker/containerd events (ETA 2h)
- Tess: run failure replay against fallback model to confirm quality (ETA 3h)
- Mike: verify nodepool autoscaling metrics and add a soft limit to prevent scale-to-zero (ETA 4h)
Assigning owners in pager system now.
oncall-bot: Pager duty updated: next_primary=Mike S, next_secondary=Tess R, handoff_confirmed_by=Alyssa
Alyssa: quick note for postmortem: suspected root cause = interplay of aggressive autoscaler + node-level memory reclaim triggering kv-cache leader eviction. We'll include hypothesis tests in the postmortem.
Tess R: customer comms status: sent initial incident note to affected customers, support follow-ups scheduled.
Mike S: for the handoff doc I'm adding a short checklist under /handbooks/oncall/handoffs/ (will link here once added).
Alyssa: outstanding risk: if autoscaler policy reverts or node re-add goes bad, traffic could spike again. If 5xx > 1% reopen pager immediately.
Praveen K: logs I've started pushing to incident artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/incidents/1769987654/logs (kernel, kubelet, edge traces).
Alyssa: final handoff notes to Mike S — check: 1) autoscaler minReplicas still 4 (dont change without coord), 2) nodepool-emb-3 drained nodes removed from LB, 3) revert fallback only when tail p95 <= 150ms for 30m.
Mike S: got it, will validate and flag any regression.
Alyssa: thanks team — marking this thread as the official handoff. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
